newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swisscargo to up ex-Germany rates March 1.
newsitem.headline: Swisscargo to up ex-Germany rates March 1.

text.p: Swisscargo Ltd, the cargo arm of Swissair, said it would raise many ex-Germany air cargo rates by up to 10 percent from March 1.
But changes to the airline's official rates would be varied by destination with some rates frozen at current levels, it added.
Swisscargo said on January 24 that ex-Switzerland rates would rise 15 centimes per kg on average from March 1 and price adjustments were planned in other European countries.
The carrier's general cargo manager Germany, Ulf Steinmann, told Reuters that the increase, in line with a general round of official airline rates rises, had met acceptance from cargo agents.
"I feel rates are picking up on the market at present," he said.
Steinmann said Swisscargo had virtually doubled rates to Delhi and Bombay in line with the substantial rates rises by other European airlines.
Rates to Hong Kong would go up 10 percent but would be kept stable to other Asian destinations.
Swisscargo would lift rates on North Atlantic routes by 5-10 percent according to destination, Steinmann said.
South America rates would rise by about 10 percent, he added.
Rates to Africa had increased by high percentage figures partially to bring them up to higher Sabena rates levels, Steinmann said.
Swisscargo has been responsible for sales and marketing of Sabena freight capacity since January 1. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
